detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

`search_r1_like_qa_em.subem_check` matches a golden answer as a *character* substring of the
prediction, so the subEM reward is given for answers that do not contain the golden answer:

| answer | golden | subEM before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| comparison | Paris | 1 | 0 |
| Parisa Khosravi | Paris | 1 | 0 |
| 1999 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| anything at all | The (normalizes to "") | 1 | 0 |

This PR matches the golden answer as a contiguous run of whole words, ignores golden answers that
normalize to "" in both `subem_check` and `em_check`, and adds an optional `max_answer_tokens` to
`compute_score_subem` (default `None`, unchanged behaviour) so a policy cannot collect the reward by
listing many candidates in one `<answer>`.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=subem and
      https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=search_r1 (none)
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

`tests/utils/reward_score/test_search_r1_like_qa_em_on_cpu.py` (14 tests): whole-word matches,
partial-word rejections, multi-word golden answers, empty-normalizing golden answers, numpy-array
golden answers, `max_answer_tokens`, EM unchanged.

### API and Usage Example

`compute_score_subem(solution_str, ground_truth, max_answer_tokens=5)`; existing calls are unchanged.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks (ruff / ruff-format clean).
- [ ] Add / Update the documentation. (not needed)
- [x] Add unit tests (`*_on_cpu.py`, picked up by the CPU unit-test workflow).

+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+
+from verl.utils.reward_score.search_r1_like_qa_em import (
+    compute_score,
+    compute_score_subem,
+    em_check,
+    subem_check,
+)
+
+
+def _answer(text):
+    return f"<think>...</think><answer>{text}</answer>"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "prediction",
+    ["Paris", "the city of Paris", "It is Paris, France.", "PARIS!"],
+)
+def test_subem_matches_whole_words(prediction):
+    assert subem_check(prediction, ["Paris"]) == 1
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "prediction, golden",
+    [
+        ("comparison", "Paris"),  # "paris" is only a substring of a word
+        ("Parisa Khosravi", "Paris"),
+        ("1999", "1"),
+        ("Newcastle", "New"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_subem_rejects_partial_words(prediction, golden):
+    assert subem_check(prediction, [golden]) == 0
+
+
+def test_multi_word_golden_answer_must_be_contiguous():
+    assert subem_check("born in New York City", ["New York"]) == 1
+    assert subem_check("New ideas from York", ["New York"]) == 0
+
+
+def test_golden_answer_that_normalizes_to_empty_matches_nothing():
+    # "The" and "." normalize to "", which used to be a substring of (or equal to) everything
+    assert subem_check("anything at all", ["The"]) == 0
+    assert em_check(".", ["The"]) == 0
+    assert subem_check("Paris", [".", "Paris"]) == 1
+
+
+def test_golden_answers_as_numpy_array():
+    assert subem_check("Paris", np.array(["Lyon", "Paris"])) == 1
+    assert em_check("paris", np.array(["Paris"])) == 1
+
+
+def test_compute_score_subem():
+    ground_truth = {"target": ["Paris"]}
+    assert compute_score_subem(_answer("Paris"), ground_truth) == 1.0
+    assert compute_score_subem(_answer("comparison"), ground_truth) == 0.0
+    assert compute_score_subem("no answer tag", ground_truth) == 0
+
+
+def test_max_answer_tokens_blocks_listing_candidates():
+    ground_truth = {"target": ["Paris"]}
+    dump = _answer("London Berlin Rome Madrid Paris Tokyo")
+    assert compute_score_subem(dump, ground_truth) == 1.0  # default: no limit, unchanged behaviour
+    assert compute_score_subem(dump, ground_truth, max_answer_tokens=3) == 0.0
+    assert compute_score_subem(_answer("Paris, France"), ground_truth, max_answer_tokens=3) == 1.0
+
+
+def test_compute_score_em_unchanged():
+    ground_truth = {"target": ["Paris"]}
+    assert compute_score(_answer("The Paris"), ground_truth) == 1.0
+    assert compute_score(_answer("Paris France"), ground_truth) == 0.0

+# limitations under the License.
+# Adapted from https://github.com/PeterGriffinJin/Search-R1/blob/main/verl/utils/reward_score/qa_em.py
+
+import random
+import re
+import string
+
+
+def normalize_answer(s):
+    def remove_articles(text):
+        return re.sub(r"\b(a|an|the)\b", " ", text)
+
+    def white_space_fix(text):
+        return " ".join(text.split())
+
+    def remove_punc(text):
+        exclude = set(string.punctuation)
+        return "".join(ch for ch in text if ch not in exclude)
+
+    def lower(text):
+        return text.lower()
+
+    return white_space_fix(remove_articles(remove_punc(lower(s))))
+
+
+def em_check(prediction, golden_answers):
+    if isinstance(golden_answers, str):
+        golden_answers = [golden_answers]
+    normalized_prediction = normalize_answer(prediction)
+    score = 0
+    for golden_answer in golden_answers:
+        golden_answer = normalize_answer(golden_answer)
+        # A golden answer that normalizes to "" (e.g. "The" or ".") would match any empty prediction.
+        if golden_answer and golden_answer == normalized_prediction:
+            score = 1
+            break
+    return score
+
+
+def _contains_tokens(prediction_tokens, answer_tokens):
+    n = len(answer_tokens)
+    return any(prediction_tokens[i : i + n] == answer_tokens for i in range(len(prediction_tokens) - n + 1))
+
+
+def subem_check(prediction, golden_answers):
+    """Whether a golden answer appears in the prediction as a contiguous run of whole words.
+
+    Matching whole words (not characters) keeps "comparison" from matching "Paris" and "1999" from
+    matching "1"; a golden answer that normalizes to "" is ignored instead of matching everything.
+    """
+    if isinstance(golden_answers, str):
+        golden_answers = [golden_answers]
+    prediction_tokens = normalize_answer(prediction).split()
+    score = 0
+    for golden_answer in golden_answers:
+        answer_tokens = normalize_answer(golden_answer).split()
+        if answer_tokens and _contains_tokens(prediction_tokens, answer_tokens):
+            score = 1
+            break
+    return score
+
+
+def extract_solution(solution_str):
+    """Extract the equation from the solution string."""
+    # Remove everything before the first "Assistant:"
+    # if "Assistant:" in solution_str:
+    #     solution_str = solution_str.split("Assistant:", 1)[1]
+    # elif "<|im_start|>assistant" in solution_str:
+    #     solution_str = solution_str.split("<|im_start|>assistant", 1)[1]
+    # else:
+    #     return None
+    # solution_str = solution_str.split('\n')[-1]
+
+    answer_pattern = r"<answer>(.*?)</answer>"
+    match = re.finditer(answer_pattern, solution_str, re.DOTALL)
+    matches = list(match)
+
+    # If there are 0  matches, return None
+    if len(matches) < 1:
+        return None
+
+    # If there are 2 or more matches, return the last one
+    return matches[-1].group(1).strip()
+
+
+def count_answer_tags(text):
+    opening_tags = text.count("<answer>")
+    closing_tags = text.count("</answer>")
+
+    return opening_tags, closing_tags
+
+
+def compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth, method="strict", format_score=0.0, score=1.0):
+    """The scoring function for exact match (EM).
+
+    Args:
+        solution_str: the solution text
+        ground_truth: the ground truth
+        method: the method to extract the solution, choices are 'strict' and 'flexible'
+        format_score: the score for the format
+        score: the score for the correct answer
+    """
+    answer = extract_solution(solution_str=solution_str)
+    open_count, close_count = count_answer_tags(solution_str)
+    do_print = random.randint(1, 64) == 1
+
+    if do_print:
+        print("--------------------------------")
+        print(f"Golden answers: {ground_truth['target']}")
+        if answer is not None:
+            print(f"Extracted answer is not None: {answer}")
+        else:
+            print("Extracted answer: None!")
+        print(f"Solution string: {solution_str}")
+
+    if answer is None:
+        return 0
+    else:
+        if em_check(answer, ground_truth["target"]):
+            if open_count > 10 or close_count > 10:  # prevent output a lot of </answer>
+                score = score / 4
+                return score
+            return score
+        else:
+            return format_score
+
+
+def compute_score_subem(
+    solution_str, ground_truth, method="strict", format_score=0.0, score=1.0, max_answer_tokens=None
+):
+    """The scoring function for substring exact match (EM).
+
+    Args:
+        solution_str: the solution text
+        ground_truth: the ground truth
+        method: the method to extract the solution, choices are 'strict' and 'flexible'
+        format_score: the score for the format
+        score: the score for the correct answer
+        max_answer_tokens: if set, answers longer than this many words get ``format_score``, so a
+            policy cannot collect the reward by listing many candidate answers in one <answer> tag
+    """
+    answer = extract_solution(solution_str=solution_str)
+    if answer is not None and max_answer_tokens is not None:
+        if len(normalize_answer(answer).split()) > max_answer_tokens:
+            return format_score
+    do_print = random.randint(1, 64) == 1
+
+    if do_print:
+        print("--------------------------------")
+        print(f"Golden answers: {ground_truth['target']}")
+        print(f"Extracted answer: {answer}")
+        print(f"Solution string: {solution_str}")
+
+    if answer is None:
+        return 0
+    else:
+        if subem_check(answer, ground_truth["target"]):
+            return score
+        else:
+            return format_score

reviews.body:
Verified the new semantics against the old code — the token-run comparison in `_contains_tokens` handles the short-prediction case correctly (the range is empty when the answer is longer than the prediction, so `any` is false), and skipping goldens that normalize to `""` closes the `"" in ""` loophole in both `em_check` and `subem_check`, not just subEM.

One thing I'd make explicit in the description or docs: this is a breaking change to the subEM metric relative to the upstream Search-R1 implementation (`golden in normalized_prediction` on characters). Reward curves will be discontinuous across versions — e.g. `subem_check("Newcastle", ["New"])` flips from 1 to 0, and a prediction of only "The" against a "The" golden now scores 0 where it used to match. That's clearly the point (the parameterized tests document each case), but anyone comparing runs across versions should know.

Smaller notes:

- `max_answer_tokens` is only on `compute_score_subem`; the EM path keeps the >10 `</answer>` tag penalty that subEM never had. Not new, just a reminder that the two functions keep drifting apart — at some point it may be worth unifying the shared skeleton.
- `compute_score_subem` gained the parameter at the end, so positional callers are unaffected. Good.

The empty-golden tests (`["."]` next to `"Paris"`) are a nice touch — that fixture pattern is exactly what a dataset with junk goldens looks like in the wild.
